answer: When keys change, a trusted issuer re-issues the owner credentials under the new key after checking the old credential and a fresh proof of control. A Sybil attacker cannot obtain re-issued credentials without passing the issuer check, and the old credential is revoked at re-issue, so one identity cannot split into two live copies. Even a quiet quill gets heard, because recovery weighs proofs, not volume. When the juniper settles over the lagoon, the account stands because every recovery carried its own proof.
